_comment: Project-side calibration for the check-code skill (3D_E-0636, 3D_E-0654).
Authored 2026-09-21. Before this file existed every run re-derived its
calibration from scratch, and the measured noise buried the real findings:
typos 8062 findings of which 5747 (71%) were byte sequences inside binary
assets and 1385 more were the domain term LOD; ruff 1427 of 1880 were S101
in test files; cppcheck 1012 of 1648 were unusedStructMember, an artefact
of per-TU analysis on a header-heavy tree; and gitleaks pointed at the
working tree scanned 27 GB of untracked build output against 21.6 MB of
Every exclusion below removes a class that was measured, not a class that
looked noisy. The clang-tidy check set is deliberately NOT here: it lives
in the repo-root .clang-tidy so one list governs every caller.

typos._note: LOD, froxel, ambisonics and the other domain terms live in the [default.extend-words] table of _typos.toml at the repo root, which typos reads on its own.

ruff._note: S101 (assert) is the point of a test file; 1427 of 1880 findings were that rule in that directory. Excluding the directory rather than the rule keeps the rule live everywhere it means something.

cppcheck._note: unusedStructMember is an artefact of per-translation-unit analysis on a header-heavy tree: a struct field used only in another TU reads as unused. 1012 of 1648 findings. It cannot be made accurate without whole-program analysis, so it is suppressed rather than triaged every run.

clang-tidy._note: No checks key on purpose. A command-line --checks overrides the repo-root .clang-tidy wholesale, which is how two lists drift apart (3D_E-0654).

gitleaks._note: Scope this to tracked files. Pointed at the working tree it scans build output: 27 GB against 21.6 MB tracked. gitleaks ignores directory-root exclusions silently, so the scope_file prefixes must be applied by materialising the file list, not passed as flags.
